headline: Tesla builds last-ever Model S and Model X at Fremont — factory line now converting to Optimus production; Fremont line targeting 1M robots/year at full capacity; Signature Edition final delivery event for existing reservation holders originally set May 12 but has since been postponed; end of Tesla's flagship luxury EV era marks the beginning of its robotics-first manufacturing era (evxl.co / notateslaapp / Electrek / TeslaNorth)

TSLA closes at $428.35 on May 8 (+4.02%) — 4-week high; strongest single-session gain since April; driven by resilient April jobs report lifting all risk assets (SPY +0.83%, QQQ +2.34%), China April deliveries +36% YoY, and ongoing Intel 14A/Terafab chip partnership narrative; stock recovered ~15% from post-earnings $373 low in under 3 weeks (primaryignition.com / stockanalysis.com)

Austin robotaxi fleet hits 52 active vehicles + 38 Cybercabs in test fleet; unsupervised ride rate surges to 59% — up from 27.8% on May 6; operational maturity accelerating sharply; 23 of 39 rides last 7 days completed with no safety driver; Cybercab test fleet size doubling signals imminent commercial integration (robotaxitracker.com)

EU FSD bloc-wide approval confirmed July at earliest, October more realistic — TCMV has no vote scheduled this week; Tesla needs representatives of 15/27 EU member states AND 65% of bloc population to vote yes; Nordic regulators (Sweden, Finland, Denmark, Norway) raised concerns over FSD allowing speeding and hands-free driving on icy roads at Brussels session; Tesla's internal target of Q2/Q3 2026 EU-wide approval now under material uncertainty (Reuters / Ars Technica / Automotive World)

Tesla begins internal testing of FSD v14.3.2 in China — first concrete testing milestone after repeated regulatory delays; Q3 2026 approval now cited as official target after missing Q1 and Q2 windows; Tesla building Baidu HD map integration per Beijing requirement that foreign firms not conduct independent HD mapping in China; only partial public-road test authorization held; China represents Tesla's largest untapped FSD subscriber market (eletric-vehicles.com / letsdatascience)

SpaceX formally files plan revealing Terafab chip factory costs $55B–$119B — joint Tesla/SpaceX semiconductor facility in Texas enters formal planning phase; research fab at Giga Texas (~$3B) will produce AI5-class chips in small batches; full Terafab scope $55B minimum with total exceeding $119B; Intel 14A process confirmed; SpaceX filing notes 'no assurance' on timeline execution; one of the largest private infrastructure investments in history if fully built

WattEV orders 370 Tesla Semi trucks in a landmark $100M deal — California's largest-ever single electric truck order; 50 trucks deliver in 2026 with full fleet by end 2027; 300+ units to support Port of Oakland freight electrification; WattEV CEO cited Tesla Semi's 'cost, performance, and availability' as decisive factors vs. competitors; signals major fleet-scale enterprise adoption accelerating alongside Gigafactory Nevada volume ramp (Teslarati / ACT Expo)

EU FSD adoption surges — Dutch users alone drive 10M km in first month after Netherlands RDW approval; one city in one country generating more FSD miles than most national fleets combined; signals explosive European subscriber uptake ahead of summer EU-wide vote; Tesla ending one-time purchase option in Netherlands May 15, funneling new EU owners into €99/month ARR pipeline
